deep.reconstruction:
This page contains no mathematical derivation. It is the opening of a draft in epistemology and philosophy of nature. It is headed 'Riemann 18', and the archive foliation is 130.

Section I (left column): 'When is our conception of the world true?' Answer, in quotation marks: 'When the connection (Zusammenhang) of our representations corresponds to the connection of things.' The elements of our picture (Bild) of the world are entirely different from the elements of the depicted real: the former are something in us, the latter something outside us. But the connections between elements in the picture must agree with the connections in what is depicted, if the picture is to be true. A deleted variant ties this agreement to 'size relations' (Grössenverhältnisse).

Section II on the truth of the picture (left column, continued in the right column):
- The truth of a picture does not depend on how fine it is. An element of the picture may represent a larger or smaller amount of the real.
- But the connections must correspond. One may not assume a direct (unmittelbare) interaction between two elements of the picture where reality has only an indirect (mittelbare) one. If two picture elements act directly on each other in that way, the picture is false and needs correction.
- Refinement is different. An element of the picture may be replaced by a group of finer elements. Its properties are then derived partly from simpler properties of the finer elements and partly from their connection, and so become partly comprehensible. This increases our insight into the connection of things, but the earlier conception need not be declared false.

Right column, bottom: a heavily cancelled question, 'From what is the connection of things to be found?' Its struck-through answers mention the sense-world, the faculty of knowing, and the representations and their diversity in space and time.

Next section, 'What is given?' (left column): Given are the external perceptions or sensations and their fusion into pictures. Every representation, as it enters as sensation, links in three ways:
1. with those already in consciousness, which gives it a place in time;
2. with those given simultaneously, which gives it a place in space;
3. with those whose reproduction it occasions, directly or indirectly, which gives it a place in the realm of concepts.
Spatial apprehension therefore rests not merely on what is given or on the linking of simultaneous data. The following page continues with Herbart's early-childhood laws of representation versus innate forms of intuition.

Context: these are the 'Erkenntnisstheoretisches' fragments printed by Weber and Dedekind in Riemann's Gesammelte Werke (1876, 'Fragmente philosophischen Inhalts'). The next page reaches the programme 'from the connection of appearances, find the connection of things', with quantitative relations as the only admissible basis.
errors: No mathematical errors are possible on this page; it contains only philosophical argument.

Conceptually consistent. Note a tension: 'truth independent of fineness' rules out false direct interactions. That presupposes Riemann's contiguous-action (Nahwirkung) ideal, which supports his later preference for mediated action over action at a distance.

results.what: Picture (Bild) theory of knowledge: a representation is true iff the connections among its elements correspond to the connections among the real things. The elements themselves need not resemble the things.
results.modern_name: Structural correspondence / picture theory (Bildtheorie); structural realism
results.usually_credited_to: Heinrich Hertz, Prinzipien der Mechanik (1894) introduction; also Helmholtz (sign theory, 1860s-1878); later Wittgenstein's Tractatus

results.what: Refinement principle: replacing a picture element by a structured group of finer elements, whose properties partly derive from their connections, deepens insight without falsifying the coarser picture. A picture that posits immediate interaction where reality has only mediated interaction is false.
results.modern_name: Reduction / theory refinement via micro-structure; contiguous action (Nahwirkung) as a criterion
results.usually_credited_to: Discussed in 19th-century German epistemology (Herbart, Helmholtz, Hertz)

results.what: Threefold association of representations: with prior representations giving temporal place, with simultaneous ones giving spatial place, and with reproduced ones giving conceptual place.
results.modern_name: Herbartian associationist psychology of space and time

deep.surprise_reason: The text is the known 'Erkenntnisstheoretisches' fragment, published in Riemann's Werke (1876). Its anticipation of Hertz's picture theory has been remarked by historians. No mathematics is involved.
transcription_corrections: Section numbers on the page appear as Roman numerals 'I.' and 'II.' rather than '1.' and '2.'.
The right-column question 'Worauf soll ... gefunden werden?' seems numbered 'II.', not '4.'.
The marginal '130' is the archive foliation.

Right-column opening 'Wenn zwei Elemente im Bilde / im Bilde ...' is garbled: the duplicated 'im Bilde' is a struck/rewritten line. The sense is: if two elements in the picture are taken to exert direct action on one another (where reality has only mediated action), the picture is false and needs correction.

'Elemente des Bildes können [?] grössere oder kleinere Mengen des Realen repräsentiren' should read as dependent on 'ob die Elemente des Bildes grössere oder kleinere Mengen ... repräsentiren' (the 'können' is likely a slip of the transcription).
In 'Gegeben sind die äusseren ... Wahrnehmungen und Empfindungen', the insertion order is uncertain; the published Werke text should be consulted.
